newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-LATE TRY GIVES MANLY TWO-POINT WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-LATE TRY GIVES MANLY TWO-POINT WIN.

text.p: Title-favourites Manly stole a try eight minutes from time to beat Sydney City 16-14 in an Australian Rugby League (ARL) play-off match on Sunday.

Manly, who topped the ARL standings at the end of regular season matches, now have a week off under the complicated play-off system while Sydney City go into a sudden-death meeting with St George next Sunday.
Under the system, the top four teams in the league all have a second chance of qualification for the second round of the knock-out stage, even if they lose their first play-off.
Teams finishing outside the top four go straight into sudden-death play-offs and are eliminated if defeated.
Manly finished top of the league, ahead of Brisbane in second, North Sydney third and Sydney City fourth.

Manly trailed 10-14 after Sydney City's Australia captain Brad Fittler scored a clever individual try midway through the second half, but with eight minutes to go centre Craig Innes crossed to score Manly's winning try.

Sydney City pressed the Manly line in the final minutes and lock Shane Rigon was unlucky not to score. He appeared to be held back by an opponent after charging down a Manly kick close to their try-line.
In the other top-four tie, North Sydney beat Brisbane 21-16 on Saturday.
Michael Buettner scored two tries for North Sydney -- his second giving his side a 19-6 lead -- before Brisbane closed the gap with two tries in the second half.
Brisbane now meet Cronulla, who finished fifth in the league and beat Western Suburbs 20-12 in their play-off on Friday thanks to two tries in the final 10 minutes.
In the other top sudden-death match, St George came from behind to eliminate 1994 champions Canberra 16-14. St George had finished seventh in the league, one place behind Canberra.
Lock Wayne Bartrim scored 12 of St George's 16 points with a try and four goals.
Canberra fought back to lead 14-10 with nine minutes left before St George centre Mark Bell crossed to level the score. Bartrim then calmly converted from the sideline to seal the win.
